memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The man said, "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called 'woman,' for she was taken out of man." — Gen 2:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are the first words a human being ever speaks in the Bible—and remarkably, they come out as poetry. After naming animal after animal and finding no true match, the man now looks upon the woman God has brought to him and bursts into joyful recognition: "This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh!" You can almost hear the relief and delight in his voice. At last, here is someone who shares his very nature—someone who belongs.

The phrase "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh" was a way of saying, "This one is truly my own kind." It speaks of deep belonging and kinship. Where the animals were unlike him, the woman is gloriously like him—his equal, his partner, sharing the same humanity.

There is something tender here about how God meets our deepest longings. Adam had felt his aloneness; now that longing gives way to joy. When God fills a need, He often does so in a way that draws worship and wonder from our hearts.

This joyful belonging points to something greater. Just as Adam recognised the woman as his own, Christ calls His people His own, sharing our very humanity so that He might redeem us (Heb 2:14). We who were once far off are now brought near and belong to Him. In Christ, no one who comes to Him is left alone or unclaimed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you known the joy of belonging, and have you thanked God for it?
- How does it feel to know that Christ claims you as His own?
- Where might God be turning a longing in your life into unexpected joy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that You meet our deepest longings and give us the joy of belonging. Thank You most of all that in Christ I am claimed as Your own. Fill my heart with wonder at Your goodness. Amen.
